facts: The judgment was delivered by V.S. Sirpurkar, J.
Ramesh and Another; (2) Mani Ram; (3) Ram Kuma v State of Uttar Pradesh
Criminal Appeal No. 184 of 2005, Criminal Appeal No. 364 of 2005 and Criminal Appeal No. 548 of 2005
The appellants were convicted for the offences u/s. 302 read with Section 149, 147 and 148 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860
The deceased Raj Kumar was the real brother of Prithvi Raj (PW-1), the complainant
There was some enmity between the family of the accused and the family of the deceased
On the fateful day, i.e., 24.10.1978, Raj Kumar (deceased) went to his tubewell, which is at about 100-125 paces from his house

The moment they reached near the Neem tree situated at a distance of 15 paces from the house of the deceased, all the accused accosted him, surrounded him and dragged him by pulling near the well upto a distance of 10-15 paces
issues: Whether the prosecution stood on the basis of interested witnesses like Prahlad (PW-4) and Daya Wati (PW-5)
Whether there was enough support in corroborating evidence
Whether the medical evidence was enough to prove the guilt
petitioner_arguments: The defence severally criticized the non-examination of the other two witnesses, namely, Rajendra Singh and Surendra, who were admittedly present
It was further urged before the High Court that the story of the FIR having been recorded at 6.30 p.m. was a myth and in fact, the FIR was ante-dated
respondent_arguments: The prosecution stood on the basis of the interested witnesses like Prahlad (PW-4) and Daya Wati (PW-5)
There was enough support in corroborating evidence
The medical evidence was enough to prove the guilt
court_reasoning: We find that both the Courts have, in a most balanced manner, appreciated the evidence of these two witnesses.
Merely because Prahlad (PW-4) was not from the same village, it cannot be said that he had no business in the village.
It is also not necessary that Prahlad (PW-4) should have straightaway gone only to the shop of the seeds and purchased the seeds.
holding: The conviction came to be confirmed by the High Court
We are convinced that the eye-witnesses are truthful and were rightly believed by the High Court.
All the six accused persons came to be convicted
cases_cited: the law laid down by this Court in Ram Lakhan Singh and Ors. Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh
